context: The XUV700 has been Mahindra's flagship since its October 2021 launch and disrupted the full-size SUV segment by pricing at 40 to 50% below equivalent-feature Toyota Fortuner and MG Gloster trims. That launch pricing is now a resale drag: rupee depreciation is steep on the top-end AX7 L trims because the new-car ceiling has not moved much through 2026.

Percentage retention on the base MX and AX3 trims is strong, well above segment average, because these were priced aggressively at launch and demand for value-end full-size SUVs is deep in tier-2 and tier-3 India. AX3 and AX5 3-year retention beats Fortuner by 4 to 5 percentage points despite the Fortuner's stronger brand equity.

Diesel XUV700 holds value 5 to 7 percentage points better than petrol at three years. The 2.2L mHawk diesel has a solid reliability record after the initial 2022 batch was updated. Automatic diesel trims (AX5 AT and above) are the highest-liquidity permutation.

The March 2026 MY26 refresh added new features (ADAS improvements, updated infotainment, new AWD calibration) but did not change the platform. Pre-MY26 units (2021 to 2025) have re-rated downwards by 3 to 4% since, a smaller drop than a full facelift would trigger.
AWD variants (available only on top-end Diesel AT trims) trade 4 to 6% above equivalent 2WD units in NCR and Bengaluru, and are broadly flat in other metros.
commonIssues: AdrenoX infotainment freeze on 2022 to early-2023 units before the October 2023 firmware update. Verify software version at inspection, dealer flash is free.
6-speed AT harshness on 2022 first-batch units, updated via TCU recalibration campaign in mid-2023. Verify service history for the fix.
Rear axle boom noise on 2022 to 2023 AWD units above 40,000 km, characteristic of the drivetrain, but budget 15,000 to 22,000 rupees for diff-mount replacement around 70,000 km.
Front suspension bush wear at 55,000 to 70,000 km, particularly on cars driven on poor roads. Routine replacement, ₹8,000 to ₹12,000 at authorised service.
Panoramic sunroof drainage clog on units driven in tree-heavy areas. Routine cleaning solves it, if ignored causes headliner water stains. Inspect closely.

faq.q: What is the resale value of a Mahindra XUV700 in India?
faq.a: A well-maintained XUV700 retains approximately 76% of its ex-showroom price after two years, 68% after three years, and 53% after five years. For a 2022 AX5 diesel with 25,000 to 50,000 km, the current fair-market band is roughly ₹12.90 to ₹15.00 lakh.

faq.q: Does the XUV700 hold value better than the Toyota Fortuner?
faq.a: In percentage terms yes for AX3 and AX5 trims, in rupee terms no. AX5 3-year retention beats the Fortuner by 4 to 5 percentage points on percentage retention, but the Fortuner's higher ex-showroom price means its absolute rupee residual is significantly higher. On top-end AX7 L trims, retention is closer to segment average.

faq.q: Is the top-end AX7 L XUV700 worth buying used?
faq.a: Yes, if you can find a 2022 to 2023 unit at a 30 to 35% discount to new. The AX7 L was priced aggressively at launch, and rupee depreciation has been steep on this trim because the new-car ceiling has not moved much. Verify the ADAS calibration and AWD system at inspection.

faq.q: Which city gives the best resale for an XUV700?
faq.a: Bengaluru and Mumbai currently trade at approximately +4 to +5% above the national mid, driven by strong SUV demand in the IT-corridor and tight used-car supply. Kolkata trades at −2%.

faq.q: How much does an XUV700 depreciate per year?
faq.a: Roughly 14% in year one, 10% additional in year two, 8% in year three, then 7 to 8% per year through year five. The five-year retention of 53% is 5 percentage points above the full-size SUV segment average of 48%.
